This integral doesn't look like one of the basic ones. However, we can manipulate the numerator a bit  to make it look more like the denominator, which reveals a more familiar expression: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}-7}{{x}^{2}+1} & =\frac{{x}^{2}+1-1-7}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}+1)-8}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{x}^{2}+1}}{\cancel{{x}^{2}+1}}-\frac{8}{{x}^{2}+1} \\  & =1-\frac{8}{{x}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Remembering that

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\text{d}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C,
$$

we can now calculate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x)=\int {f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (1-\frac{8}{{x}^{2}+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \text{d}x-\int \frac{8}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \text{d}x-8\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x-8\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
